lines: I need the Department of Higher Education.
Tab to About. Down arrow. Where did the link go?
I turn on Curb Cut. Same menu. Same keyboard.
There it is. The D H E.
Kane tries the same task with a mouse. The department page opens.
With keys alone, Kane cannot reach that link. Now we have a reproducible failure.
Here’s a failure that went straight back to the coding agent. Watch the converter’s answer field.
At this width, the field runs off the screen.
Codex receives Kane’s failed assertion and writes a rule to stack the cells.
Kane runs it again. One meter. The answer is visible.
At Munich Airport, listen to the previous slide control.

@Anna|Vorherige Folie.

The site owner gets the task, the recordings, and a source repair.
One hundred five fixes are live. Get Curb Cut for Chrome.
On ExtremeTerrain, the Details link is faint. Curb Cut adjusts its contrast and measures the result.
Let’s look at what Kane actually checked. On Mass dot E D U, the target is a specific department page.
The tester gets a keyboard and the same destination. Down arrow leaves About focused. The link underneath stays hidden.
In the pointer control, hover reveals the link. Following it confirms that the destination exists.
The installed rule gives focus the same behavior as hover. With that rule, Kane follows the link using only keys.
For the converter, we can trace the handoff to a single failed run.
Its identifier travels with the assertion into the coding agent’s repair record.
The agent changes the layout of the table and its cells. Now the result fits a three hundred twenty pixel viewport.
For developers, curb cut check is the entry point. The intended loop runs the task, gives the agent Kane’s reason, and tests its next change.
Curb cut gate brings the same check into a coding agent’s stop hook. A failing task sends the agent back to the source.
In the trust popup, the visitor can inspect the verification status and play the supporting recording.
Jev’s public test found names on seven sites. Thirteen of fifteen applied names were judged correct. Two were too vague.
A visitor can report another barrier from the keyboard, at the point where the task breaks.
For the About menu, the report recommends applying the hover styling when focus moves inside the menu. The owner can fix the source.
The nightly local check repeats the task. Public Kane rechecks also run without and with the patch. An inconclusive run preserves the last verified state.
Once the unpatched task passes, Curb Cut retires its rule. The site now carries the repair for everyone.
Install Curb Cut for Chrome. Open the proof for a fix, replay the task, and see where your next key takes you.
